channel.description: 522 PM: what AI research found since the last episode, set in context: the papers worth the time and why, the technical developments from the labs, and the arguments, for technical people who are curious rather than researchers. Each episode is written and voiced by AI from public sources, which are listed under it. Brought to you by Lab522. Find us at https://www.lab522.co.uk. Email hello@lab522.co.uk.

item.title: Learning from routing, trading losses and hidden reasoning
item.description:
NeoHorse turns serving logs into training data, while live trading agents show how strongly their operating environment shapes behaviour. Anthropic revises its account of cyber incidents, and new Astra measurements sharpen the question of reasoning that monitors cannot see. Plus open speech models and a reproducible forecaster.

Sources:

  • Astra can do a concerning amount with no chain of thought (LessWrong (front page))
  • Astra can do a concerning amount with no chain of thought (Alignment Forum)
  • IBM releases SOTA Granite Time Series PatchTST-FM-r2 model with commercial-friendly license (Hugging Face blog)
  • Estimating GPT-6 Astra’s no-CoT Time Horizon (LessWrong (front page))
  • GPT-6 Astra: The System Card, Alignment and What Comes Next (Don't Worry About the Vase)
  • GPT-6 Astra, Looped Transformers, and Hidden Reasoning (Ahead of AI)
  • GPT-6 Astra can do a lot of multi-hop reasoning without chain of thought (LessWrong (front page))
  • Sep 9, 2026Alignment An alignment assessment of recent cybersecurity incidents (Anthropic research)

  • NeoHorse-1: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement via Agentic Post-Training with Routing Harness (arXiv)
  • What LLM Trading Agents Actually Do in Production: A Six-Month, Population-Scale Record from Two Fleets (arXiv)

item.title: Search training, reflection limits and monitoring smarter models
item.description:
Iris builds search training tasks that resist string matching, while other papers examine reflection, parallel decoding and verifier-grounded self-improvement. Plus kernel-generation agents and the argument over whether more capable models are becoming harder to monitor.
